newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC, Med rates firm in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC, Med rates firm in active trade.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) and Mediterranean rates firmed on Tuesday in active trade, brokers said.

"There has been a slight improvement...Things have definitely picked up (on VLCCs)," one broker said. He put Mideast/Japan VLCCs at W62.5, up some five points, and Mideast/west and Mideast/Singapore rates up more modestly at W52.5.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady at around W70, also in busy trade, with the 260,000 tonne Athos fixed at W70 for Shell, loading April 29.
The Suezmax (130,000 tonne) market was likewise active, with West Africa cargoes slightly firmer at W97.5 and Med cargoes up five points at W95.
"There's a lack of tonnage to the end of the month," said an Italian broker referring to the Med market.
Another broker said Med Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) enjoyed a busy day with at least eight vessels fixed this morning, pushing rates up five points to W125.
Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes, meanwhile, were steady at W100 and 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were unchanged at W180 in the north and W195 in the Med.

Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne crude rates edged up five points to W230 as tonnage thinned out, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes fell to about W180 from W195 on a good supply of prompt ships, brokers said.
